newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: CM Telecom seeks listing in Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: CM Telecom seeks listing in Hong Kong.

text.p: Singapore-listed CM Telecom International Ltd applied for a primary listing on the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong Ltd on Thursday, a company official said.

"We have submitted the application to the Hong Kong exchange today for dual primary listing in Hong Kong," Frank Wu, CM Telecom's executive director told a news conference after the release of its financial results for year ended March 31, 1997.
The telecommunication company said trading of the shares would be in Hong Kong dollars. Price and lot size would be determined at a later date.
Wu told Reuters its Hong Kong listing was to enhance the group's corporate profile in Hong Kong, its operational base, and not intended as a major fund raising exercise.
"We have applied for the Hong Kong listing without the intention of raising capital but more so to raise our corporate profile," Wu said.
He said the Hong Kong listing would cater to increasing interest from Hong Kong investors.
Wu said CM Telecom, listed in Singapore since October 17, 1996, would continue to be traded in Singapore.
He dismissed speculation the group was unhappy with the performance of its Singapore-listed stock, which has been trading below its initial public offer price of US$0.32 each.
"No, Singapore has in fact helped generated investors' interest and raised our profile," Wu said.
CM Telecom shares ended down US$0.005 at US$0.28 on 707,000 shares on Thursday.
